items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: But we did an album with Ernie Louie Henry called 'Presenting Ernie Louie Henry' -- Arthur Taylor, Kenny Dorham, [Jim Knight], or whatever.

ctx.x: Philly Billy Joe and Kenny Drew was the rhythm section; we didn't know it at that moment, because

they had -- let's see who else came in? Drew, myself, Philly filled in most of the time; yeah, A.T. a couple of times. But we did an album with Ernie Louie Henry called 'Presenting Ernie Louie Henry' -- Arthur Taylor, Kenny Dorham, [Jim Knight], or whatever. But we made that, and oh, started recording with Dick Stig Johnson, this altoist, Dave McKenna, a pianist, and Billy Joe, and who else? Oh, my goodness, I started recording with everybody they would bring in there.

I'd be downstairs, in the garage, you know, sleeping and he'd say, 'Keepnews All right Wilbur, you got a record date tomorrow -- where's your fiddle?' Now, as long as I'm working, my fiddle was around, you know, but when the office pawn it and is closed, like on a - say, if I'm not working, I'd get it out Monday morning, you know, and that was the fiddle that Oscar Pettiford gave me now, when he saw me in New York.
